title: Law enforcement accomplishments
intro: The record contains real, sourced wins, and this section reports them straight. Each entry is an agency's own account of its work, with the independent corroboration shown where one exists — and each entry says whether the number counts an outcome (lives, rescues, cases closed) or activity (arrests, seizures).

rows.claim: Violent crime down 9.3% in 2025 — the largest year-to-year decline since FBI estimation began in 1936 — with murder at 4.1 per 100,000, tied for the lowest rate ever recorded.
rows.corroboration: Independently visible in CDC death-certificate data, which registers the same turn.

rows.claim: Overdose deaths fell 26.2% in 2024 — the largest one-year drop on record — and kept falling in 2025. CDC attributes the decline to naloxone distribution, treatment access, shifts in supply and renewed prevention.
rows.corroboration: Reported as attributed; the mortality series itself is final vital-statistics data.

rows.what: World Cup anti-trafficking operation: 180 people rescued
rows.claim: HSI-led operations around the 2026 FIFA World Cup rescued 180 trafficking victims, 30 of them children — alongside 905 arrests of suspects.
rows.corroboration: The rescue figure is the outcome; the arrest figure counts activity, and DHS publishes no breakdown of eventual charges.

rows.what: A full year of trafficking enforcement
rows.claim: HSI initiated 1,686 sex-trafficking and forced-labour investigations in FY2024, leading to 2,545 arrests.
rows.corroboration: Agency annual report; arrest and investigation counts, not convictions.

rows.claim: The FBI put a $25,000 minimum reward on every publicly advertised unsolved homicide, kidnapping and missing-person case in Indian country, with a searchable national case map.
rows.corroboration: An institutional commitment to cases this record shows are undercounted — counted here as a commitment, not yet an outcome.

rows.claim: The share of homicides cleared returned to 61.4% in 2024, back to the 2019 level after the 52.3% low of 2022.
rows.corroboration: Corroborated via the Murder Accountability Project's compilation of FBI data; still roughly four in ten uncleared.

discipline: An accomplishment claim is the agency's account. Where a number counts activity rather than outcomes, the entry says so — an arrest or a seizure is the start of a process, not the end of one.
